answer: Each agent must lock a scarce onyx token in a public registry before it can submit work, and the token stays bonded until its contribution is audited. A jade reputation score then grows only from tasks verified by independent peers, so creating many names does not create trusted history. To flood the economy, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, paying the opportunity cost for every identity, and risks losing them when fraud is proven. A public thread links each claim to its audit.
